newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia imposes 15 pct tax on T-bill earnings.
newsitem.headline: Russia imposes 15 pct tax on T-bill earnings.

text.p: The Russian parliament extended a 15-percent income tax to earnings from operations with government securities on Wednesday and Thursday.
Treasury bills and government bonds had previously been exempt from the 15-percent tax on profits from operations with securities.

The Federation Council upper chamber of parliament approved the tax on Thursday after the State Duma lower house of parliament passed it in a third reading on Wednesday. President Boris Yeltsin must sign the bill before it becomes law.
The amendment is part of a package of tax laws which had to be approved or rejected before Saturday's third reading of the 1997 draft budget, which incorporates the taxes in revenues.
The Duma on Wednesday also rejected a bill calling for a 0.5 percent tax on cash purchases of hard currency in a second reading. It had passed the law in a first reading on December 11.
